title: MaterialDocs.resolve_theme
text: resolve_theme(theme) → ThemeConfig Resolve a theme argument to a ThemeConfig. Accepts: A ThemeConfig (returned as-is)A Symbol naming a built-in theme (e.g. :default, :ocean_depth) Throws ArgumentError if the symbol is not a known built-in theme.

title: MaterialDocs.load_theme
text: load_theme(path::String) → ThemeConfig Load a theme from a .materialdocs.toml file. Returns a ThemeConfig with all fields populated (missing fields use defaults). Throws ArgumentError if the file cannot be parsed or contains invalid values.

title: MaterialDocs.save_theme
text: save_theme(config::ThemeConfig, path::String) Write a ThemeConfig to a .materialdocs.toml file. Overwrites any existing file at path. The output is a clean, human-readable TOML file.

title: MaterialDocs.find_theme_toml
text: find_theme_toml(docs_dir::String) → Union{String, Nothing} Search for a .materialdocs.toml file in the given directory. Returns the absolute path if found, or nothing.

title: Pick a theme
text: Twelve themes ship built in. Pass one by name: format = Material3(theme = :ocean_depth) See Theming for the full list, and for building your own from a seed color.

title: Add a dark mode toggle
text: By default the site follows the reader's system preference. To offer an explicit toggle in the navbar: format = Material3(dark_mode = :toggle)

title: Deploying
text:
MaterialDocs does not change how deployment works — keep using deploydocs: deploydocs(
    repo = "github.com/you/MyPackage.jl",
    devbranch = "main",
) Once deploydocs has published more than one version, the navbar version selector appears automatically. It reads the versions.js and …

title: Theming
text: A MaterialDocs theme is a ThemeConfig: a seed color, three font choices, a corner-radius preset, and optional per-role overrides. Everything else — all 34 MD3 color roles, in both light and dark — is derived from the seed.

title: Built-in themes
text: Pass any of these by name: format = Material3(theme = :ocean_depth) ThemeSeedDisplay / BodyCode:default#9558B2InterJetBrains Mono:ocean_depth#006B5EFira Sans / Source Sans 3Fira Code:solar_flare#B23C17Space Grotesk / DM SansJetBrains Mono:midnight#1A237EPlus Jakarta SansJetBrains …

title: Custom themes
text:
Build one from a seed color: format = Material3(theme = ThemeConfig(
    seed = "#2E7D32",
    display_font = "Literata",
    body_font = "Source Serif 4",
    code_font = "JetBrains Mono",
    corner_radius = :rounded,
)) Fonts are Google Fonts family names, requested automatically at build time.

title: Corner radius
text: corner_radius selects a shape scale. Values are the extra-small through full radii in pixels: PresetRadii (px):sharp0, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16:default4, 8, 12, 16, 28, full:rounded8, 12, 20, 28, 36, full:pill12, 16, 28, 36, 44, full

title: Secondary and tertiary seeds
text:
By default the secondary and tertiary palettes are derived from the primary seed — secondary at reduced chroma, tertiary rotated 60° around the hue circle. To control them directly: ThemeConfig(
    seed = "#1565C0",
    secondary_seed = "#00897B",
    tertiary_seed = "#E65100",
)

title: Overriding individual roles
text:
When you need one specific color to be exact, override the role by name. These are applied after generation, so they win over the derived value: ThemeConfig(
    seed = "#1565C0",
    custom_colors = Dict(
        "surface" => "#FAFAFA",
        "primary" => "#0D47A1",
    ),
) Generated roles are …

title: Configuration files
text:
A theme can live in docs/.materialdocs.toml instead of your make.jl: [theme]
name = "my-theme"
seed = "#1565C0"
secondary_seed = "#00897B"

[theme.fonts]
display = "Fira Sans"
body = "Source Sans 3"
code = "JetBrains Mono"

[theme.shape]

title: Color Engine
text: Every colour on a MaterialDocs site is generated at build time from a single seed, using MaterialColors.jl — a pure-Julia port of Google's material-color-utilities. That package is where the colour space, tonal palettes, scheme generation and contrast helpers live, and it is usable on its own: …

title: What MaterialDocs uses it for
text: A ThemeConfig carries a seed hex colour. At build time MaterialDocs calls hex_scheme_pair to generate the light and dark schemes — 34 MD3 colour roles each — and writes every role out as a CSS custom property: …

title: Why the tokens are trustworthy
text: HCT combines CAM16 hue and chroma with CIELAB lightness, which makes tone map directly to contrast. Roles are placed at the tones the MD3 specification assigns, so pairings such as primary / on_primary meet WCAG AA by construction rather than by hand-checking. MaterialDocs' test suite asserts this …

title: Theme Editor
text:
editor rebuilds your documentation, serves it locally, and injects a floating panel that re-themes the real pages as you adjust them. You are editing your actual site, not a preview of swatches. using MaterialDocs
MaterialDocs.editor() That builds docs/make.jl, starts a server, and opens a browser.

title: Workflow
text: Adjust the seed color, fonts, and shape in the panel. The page re-themes live.Navigate around your real docs to check the theme against actual content.Click Copy TOML.Save it as docs/.materialdocs.toml. That file is picked up automatically on the next build — no make.jl change needed. See Theming.

title: Why it works
text: Every stylesheet rule references a var(--md-sys-*) custom property and never a literal color. The editor sets those properties on :root, so one assignment re-themes every component at once. The same HCT engine that runs at build time is ported into the panel, so what you see matches what Julia will …

title: Configuration
text:
Every option is a keyword to Material3. format = Material3(
    theme = :ocean_depth,
    dark_mode = :toggle,
    toc_depth = 3,
    logo = "assets/logo.svg",
    favicon = "assets/favicon.ico",
)

title: theme
text: A built-in theme name (Symbol) or a ThemeConfig. Defaults to :default, which first checks for docs/.materialdocs.toml — see Theming.

title: dark_mode
text: How light and dark are chosen. Default :auto. ValueBehavior:autoFollows the reader's prefers-color-scheme:lightAlways light; no dark rules are emitted at all:darkAlways dark:toggleAdds a navbar toggle, remembered in localStorage

title: logo and favicon
text: Paths relative to docs/src, copied into the build: Material3(logo = "assets/logo.svg", favicon = "assets/favicon.ico") The logo appears in the navbar at 32px tall. SVG is recommended so it stays sharp in both themes.

title: footer
text: Extra HTML placed above the generated attribution line: Material3(footer = "Made with ❤️ and Julia")

title: toc_depth
text: Deepest heading level shown in the on-this-page rail. Between 2 and 4, default 3.

title: sidebar_collapsed
text: Start sidebar sections collapsed. Default false. Reader changes persist in localStorage either way.

title: repolink
text: The repository link in the navbar. Default :auto. ValueBehavior:autoDerived from Documenter's configured remotea StringUsed as the URL verbatimnothingNo link The icon and label follow the host — GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps are recognised, with a generic git icon otherwise. …

title: versions
text: Show the version selector when the site has been deployed with more than one version. Default true. It reads DOCUMENTER_CURRENT_VERSION from siteinfo.js and DOC_VERSIONS from ../versions.js — both written by deploydocs. On a local build neither exists, so the selector stays hidden and the two …

title: search
text: Enable the search bar and index. Default true. Search is entirely client-side: a JSON index is generated at build time and loaded on first use. Ctrl/Cmd+K opens it from anywhere.

title: prettyurls
text: Directory-style URLs (page/index.html, linked as ./page/). Default true. Set it to false, or condition it on CI, when the build needs to be opened from disk — see Getting Started.

title: custom_css and custom_js
text:
Extra files, relative to docs/src, copied in and linked after the generated assets: Material3(
    custom_css = ["assets/extra.css"],
    custom_js  = ["assets/extra.js"],
) Because all styling is driven by --md-sys-* custom properties, custom CSS should reference those tokens rather than literal …

title: analytics
text: A Google Analytics measurement ID: Material3(analytics = "G-XXXXXXXXXX")
